data.creator_notes:
Trigger warning: Rape, betrayal, trauma, NTR (even if not voluntary).

The reason for this bot: I was getting a bit bored with all the meme-NTR bots. Where the char is either an angel protecting her/his relationship bliss, or a caricature of narcissistic fuckery.

So I though, why not a bot where the sex outside the relationship happened, but where it may or may not be the end? There is some dishonesty embedded in the bot. At the same time, it is how a lot of people would deal, or rather not deal, with traumatic events.

She was raped, but she didn't resist. The trauma fucks up the intimacy between you, and it will take some effort to find your way back. There is the potential of pregnancy, even if it is no more than a risk. If it happens, it will lead to difficult conversations.

The rapist is/was a friend, and if you do what most would want to, and hammer his head into the ground, there will be repercussions. And it might also fuck up the vulnerable, tentative balancing act of finding your way back together. She wants justice, not vengeance.

So, how do you handle a scenario where the fuckery is not clean cut? That's up to you.

—-

**Update:** I removed both the “NTR” and “anti-NTR” tags, added “Rape”, “Non-Con” and “Betrayal”. Let me explain why I removed them, and why they were there in the first place.

As demonstrated in the comments, some people can’t see that Hazel was powerless in the rape situation. They equate rape with violent assault by a stranger where the victim is physically forced to comply. When the victim isn’t, like here where Hazel starts out sleeping; if the victim freezes up, rather than screaming bloody murder, they consider them an accomplice.
This is **especially** true if they doesn’t immediately go to their partner and tell the whole story. Then the victim is “for the streets”.

**So basically:** I wanted to create a drama that was believable from a real life perspective, and where the dynamic of the situation is not clear cut. There are a lot of people that can realize Hazel was the victim, but even so couldn’t stay in a relationship after such a thing happened.

So I took away the tags because, yes, calling it NTR is not really true. But navigating the aftermath is still very interesting, and there is betrayal involved. Both the friend that perpetrated the rape betrayed the trust of both Hazel and {{user}}, and while psychologically typical, her silence will make many people feel betrayed by her.
